bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- IGL Spirits aspires to a debt-free operating model / debt-free balance sheet from FY28 onwards while targeting Rs 1,000 Cr EBITDA in the next 4-5 years.
- Debt levels and the debt-to-equity ratio improved during Q1FY27; the company is refinancing higher-cost borrowings with lower-cost debt to improve financial efficiency.
- Strong credit profile: A- Stable rating from CARE Ratings, with a low gearing ratio (Debt-to-Equity of 0.54x in FY26).
- Post-demerger, each of the three businesses will independently manage its own capital, investments and resources based on its specific needs, aiming for more efficient capital use.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Only producer of ethylene-based glycol ethers in India, which keeps the domestic market steady despite low-cost butyl and propyl based competition
- Only plant in India with in-house production of both EO and LCO2 used to make ETO (IGL-STERI GAS), giving a distinct edge over other suppliers
- First company in the world to develop bio-based amines derived from sustainable, renewable raw materials, engineered for cosmetics and pharmaceutical applications
- Bio-based, low-carbon-footprint product portfolio that makes it a preferred partner for multinationals with defined sustainability and UN SDG commitments
- Capability, built with international technology innovators, to convert ethanol derived from recycled industrial carbon emissions into MEG - a traceable sustainable sourcing alternative
- Strong in-house R&D and technical team, with an established R&D centre at Kashipur and a Dehradun centre for phyto APIs and nutraceuticals
- Logistics advantage of a northern location for ethylene oxide supply, where safety limits transport distance
- Grain-based distilleries at Kashipur and Gorakhpur that reduce dependence on imported ethanol; the Company is largely self-sufficient for its alcohol requirements
- Established value chain in guar-based bio-polymers, backed by India supplying nearly 80% of global guar gum demand
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Environmental and regulatory change — Identified in the BRSR as a material risk with negative implications: amendments to existing laws and the introduction of new regulations may impact raw material procurement, production processes, effluent treatment, disposal practices and manufacturing of finished products, and along with other environmental considerations could adversely affect business operations.
- Climate change and decarbonisation pressure — The Company states it continues to realign its strategies in view of challenges arising from climate change and evolving environmental concerns to ensure operational resilience, with focused internal initiatives to reduce carbon emissions and minimise the environmental footprint of its operations.
- Handling of hazardous materials — Flagged in the BRSR as a material risk with negative implications; the Company commits to safe and responsible handling of hazardous materials across its operations to protect employee health and minimise potential impact on the surrounding environment - relevant given ethylene oxide and related chemistries.
- Waste management and disposal compliance — Flagged as a material risk with negative implications; the Company assumes full responsibility for safe and compliant disposal of hazardous and non-hazardous waste, and notes that any deviation would result in legal, financial and reputational implications including fines and penalties imposed by regulatory authorities.
- Health and safety issues — Listed among the material responsible business conduct issues as a risk with negative implications for a company running continuous-process chemical, distillery and industrial gas operations.
- Cyber security — Listed in the BRSR material issues table as a risk with negative implications.
- Governance and compliance exposure — The Company notes increasing regulatory emphasis on transparency, accountability and fairness and says it is focused not only on strict adherence to existing requirements but also on proactively preparing for evolving governance norms; it relies on a Code of Conduct and Ethics Policy, Anti-Bribery policies, Whistle Blower Policy and Related Party Transactions Policy to manage this exposure.

business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- First company in the world to produce Ethylene Oxide (EO) / Mono Ethylene Glycol (MEG) from a renewable agro route based on molasses since 1989; largest bio-based specialty chemicals manufacturer and only supplier at scale globally of bio-based EO, Glycols and Glycol Ether.
- Market leader in Country Liquor in Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand; Bunty Bubli is India's highest-selling Non-IMFL brand, and Malta Whisky leads in Uttarakhand.
- Established leadership in Thiocolchicoside with strong export and domestic momentum in the Ennature Biopharma business.
- ISCC PLUS certified; positions itself as India's leading Green Chemical Company with a 100+ green product portfolio.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Demerger] NCLT sanctioned the Scheme of Arrangement on 17 July 2026: Spirits, Bio Fuel and Biopharma undertakings transfer via demerger to IGL Spirits Limited and Ennature Bio Pharma Limited respectively, while Chemicals, Bio-Glycols, New Specialty Products, Industrial Gases remain within India Glycols Limited; both resulting companies are to be listed on NSE & BSE, with promoter holding at 59.63% in each of the three companies post-restructuring. The Company has withdrawn the earlier proposed amalgamation of Kashipur Holdings Limited into IGL.
- [Partnership] 15-year-long partnership with Bacardi under which IGL manages supply chain, logistics and regulatory approvals, and bottles/supplies Bacardi brands (including Breezers, Carta Blanca, Limon) from Kashipur for North and East India; separate Amrut partnership gives IGL investment, distribution and marketing rights for select Amrut brands in North India.
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: India Glycols manufactures bio-based specialities and performance chemicals (bio-based glycols such as MEG, DEG, TEG and heavy glycols, glycol ethers and ether esters, specialty chemicals, bio-polymers, bio-based ethylene oxide and industrial gases), potable spirits comprising Indian Made Foreign Liquor, branded country liquor and Extra Neutral Alcohol, power alcohol (bio-fuel) and Ennature Biopharma products. Its output is derived from renewable feedstock rather than petrochemical routes, and it supplies multinational corporations and large enterprises with defined environmental sustainability mandates across beverages, packaging, textile fibres, paints and coatings, personal care, oil and gas, agriculture and healthcare. The company is a public company incorporated in India, listed on the NSE and BSE, with its registered office at Kashipur, Uttarakhand.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Bio-Based Specialities and Performance Chemicals:** Bio-based Glycols (MEG, DEG, TEG and Heavy Glycols), Glycol Ethers, Glycol Ether Esters, Specialty chemicals, Bio-Polymers (guar gum and derivatised guar), Bio-based Ethylene Oxide, Bio-Amines, Methyl Ester and Oil Dispersion formulations
- **Industrial Gases:** Liquid Oxygen, Liquid Argon, Beverage and Industrial Grade Liquid Carbon Dioxide (LCO2), IGL-STERI GAS (Ethylene Oxide and Carbon Dioxide gas mixtures, ETO)
- **Potable Spirits:** Indian Made Foreign Liquor (IMFL), Branded Country Liquor, Extra Neutral Alcohol (ENA)
- **Power Alcohol (Bio-Fuel):** Power Alcohol / ethanol
- **Ennature Biopharma:** Plant-derived phyto APIs, Nutraceutical ingredients

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Diversify markets geographically - strengthen presence across the Far East and Southeast Asia through strategic partnerships and innovative marketing to offset moderating demand from the United States and European markets and reduce dependence on any single market
- Build sustainability-led differentiation in bio-based MEG, including the capability developed with international technology innovators to convert ethanol derived from recycled industrial carbon emissions into MEG as a traceable sourcing alternative
- Client focus on multinational corporations and large enterprises with strong environmental sustainability mandates, supplying bio-based MEG from renewable feedstock into beverages, packaging and textile fibres
- Defend glycol ether share by adjusting pricing strategy and leveraging bio-based product attributes such as low carbon footprint and green credentials in export markets
- Broaden the performance chemicals footprint with differentiated chemistries - Bio-Amines for cosmetics, pharmaceutical, hair care and skin care applications, where commercial deliveries to global personal-care MNCs have commenced
- Expand the value-added specialty portfolio serving customer sustainability and ESG targets, including further expansion of the Oil and Gas product portfolio and a growing innovation pipeline
- Enter crop protection with Methyl Ester and its Oil Dispersion formulations as a sustainable alternative to conventional hydrocarbon solvents, and position glycols and derivatives as replacements for hazardous solvents in Emulsifiable Concentrate formulations
- Pursue strategic partnerships and innovative applications in glycol ethers to navigate a competitive landscape dominated by low-cost Chinese butyl and propyl products
- The Company funds growth through a blend of term debt and equity. During FY26 it raised fresh term loans while repaying maturing term debt and pre-paying further term loans, and raised Rs 466.99 crore through a preferential issue of equity shares which it says has strengthened its liquidity and cash flow position. It states it has been regular in meeting principal and interest obligations to banks and NBFCs, discontinued its fixed deposit scheme back in FY 2009-10 and has accepted no fresh public deposits, with no overdue deposits outstanding and nothing required to be transferred to the Investor Education and Protection Fund. On shareholder returns, the interim dividend of Rs 7.50 per equity share is being placed before the 42nd AGM for confirmation as the final dividend for the year ended 31st March 2026. Governance of capital deployment sits with the Audit Committee, whose terms of reference include monitoring the end use of funds raised through public, rights and preferential issues against the stated objects, scrutiny of inter-corporate loans and investments, and valuation of undertakings or assets, alongside a dedicated Finance Committee of the Board.
- Bio-based, low-carbon product strategy: the Company aims to deliver high-performance, low-carbon specialty chemicals that support global decarbonisation goals and to be a trusted partner for organisations pursuing net-zero emission targets
- Focused internal initiatives to reduce carbon emissions and minimise the overall environmental footprint of operations as part of realigning strategy to climate change
- Commitment to minimising environmental footprint by utilising renewable resources and optimising energy and water efficiency while improving operational excellence
- Green chemistry and eco-friendly product development, with an R&D pipeline covering products from carbon capture (C-smart alcohol), bio-based specialties replacing traditional chemicals, and green solvents including bio-esters for agriculture and specialty bio-amines for personal care
- Board gender diversity: women represent 37.50% of the Board of Directors, though 0% of Key Managerial Personnel
- Governance and ethics architecture comprising a Code of Conduct and Ethics Policy, Anti-Bribery policies, Whistle Blower Policy and Related Party Transactions Policy, with a Risk Management Committee of Board and Senior Management members overseeing identification, assessment and mitigation of key business risks through structured quarterly reviews across departments and sites
- Stakeholder grievance redressal mechanisms are in place for communities, investors, shareholders, employees and workers, customers and value chain partners, including a dedicated Grievance Redressal Committee for employees and workers
- CSR is applicable to the Company under Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013, and the Company engages with local communities through its CSR plans and activities to address their grievances
- Scientific integrity in the nutraceutical/API business: every new ingredient undergoes pharmacokinetic, toxicological and clinical evaluation using HPLC, LC-MS/MS and GC-MS platforms, adhering strictly to ICH and OECD guidelines
- BRSR reporting boundary is standalone and no external assessment or assurance provider has been engaged for the report
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The planned capex on the distillery, New Value-Added Chemical Products and the Bio-Fuel Ethanol Plant has been completed, and the Company says it is now leveraging that expanded scale and capacity for growth; strategic investments in ethanol and green energy solutions have strengthened its position in the renewable energy space and left it largely self-sufficient for its alcohol requirements. In the bio-fuel business the Company undertook a significant capacity enhancement of its ethanol plants at both Kashipur and Gorakhpur during the recent years, which it expects to strengthen its standing as a leading ethanol manufacturer and improve its ability to fulfil larger supply commitments; it has been allocated ethanol supply quantities under the Government's Ethanol Blending Programme for the third consecutive year, for the Ethanol Supply Year running from November 2025 to October 2026. The Potable Spirits segment is served by two distilleries at Kashipur, Uttarakhand and Gorakhpur, Uttar Pradesh with a combined production capacity of 3,79,000 kilolitres per annum of ethyl alcohol, of which 1,35,788 kilolitres per annum is dedicated to potable alcohol; the Kashipur facility is described as one of the most efficient distilleries in the country. In industrial gases, IGL has completed debottlenecking of its Liquid CO2 plant at Kashipur, which it expects to improve overall yield in the coming year and make larger volumes available for sale, and has invested in upgradation of quality control equipment, adopting ISO 13485:2016 for its EO-CO2 gas mixtures cylinder filling plant to help open new medical-use markets. The Company notes the industrial gas sector as a whole is in a massive capex cycle with new Oxygen and Argon capacities and Air Separation Unit additions in North and East India keeping prices in check. Funding-wise, the year's highlight was the completion of a Rs 466.99 crore capital raise through a preferential issue of 51,03,765 equity shares, which strengthened net worth and liquidity.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- The domestic MEG market is anticipated to expand at a CAGR of approximately 7-8%, significantly surpassing the global average, underpinned by robust domestic PET demand and sustained growth in textile and apparel exports
- The global MEG market is projected to expand from USD 24.16 billion in 2022 to USD 30.98 billion by 2030, a CAGR of approximately 3.2%, driven by rising polyester fibre demand in Asia-Pacific
- The Company anticipates steady and sustained growth in bio-based MEG in the years ahead as more customers adopt Bio-MEG as a credible alternative to petrochemical-based MEG
- Escalated conflict in West Asia and the Middle East disrupted MEG imports into India, hiking prices and constraining availability, while very high input costs created a demand squeeze in the end market
- The persistent price gap between petro-based MEG and bio-based MEG remains the deciding factor for new potential end users
- Changes in U.S. market policies favouring recycled PET are expected to create headwinds for the Bio-MEG sector
- Lower feedstock costs in China let Chinese manufacturers price butyl and propyl glycol ethers more competitively across Southeast Asia, compressing IGL export volumes and, as traders recalibrated to Chinese import levels, domestic realisations and margins as well
- The global glycol ethers market is projected to grow at 5.5% CAGR over the next five years, but butyl/propyl ethers are expected to capture that growth while ethylene-based ethers remain under pressure
- The domestic glycol ether market remains steady because IGL is the only producer of ethylene-based ethers in India
- Long-term outlook for the performance chemicals segment remains robust despite Middle East geopolitical tensions creating demand and supply-chain headwinds in Q4 of the financial year
- India's specialty chemicals sector is expected to grow from USD 250 billion to USD 300 billion by 2028 and USD 1 trillion by 2040, supported by demand from food processing, personal care and home care
- Premiumisation is the dominant trend reshaping India's liquor industry, with premium and luxury spirits likely to grow nearly 15% and the industry projected at 8-10% revenue growth in FY26
- Ethanol blending policy support continues - OMCs averaged 19.05% blending in 2024-25 and 19.93% in July 2025, with policy attention now turning to E25 and beyond including E85/E100 for flex-fuel vehicles
- Guar-based bio-polymer demand is supported by rising global preference for natural, clean-label additives across food, personal care, pharmaceuticals, mining, paper, textiles and oilfield applications
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Strong 63% YoY growth in biofuels revenue and 33% EBITDA growth driven by ethanol blending program, coupled with margin expansion in chemicals and spirits, while debt reduction via INR 467cr preferential allotment sets up credit rating upgrade; what matters is the confluence of policy tailwinds, premiumization momentum, and green chemical commercialization as near-term catalysts.

open.item: For the third consecutive year the Company has been allocated quantities for the supply of ethanol under the Government's Ethanol Blending Programme, for the Ethanol Supply Year from November 2025 to October 2026.
Debottlenecking of the Liquid CO2 plant at Kashipur is expected to improve overall yield in the coming year and make larger volumes available for sale.

The Board approved a Scheme of Arrangement amongst India Glycols Limited, Ennature Bio Pharma Limited and IGL Spirits Limited with their respective shareholders, involving demerger of the Bio Pharma Undertaking.
The Company is advancing its pilot facility for the development of specialty molecules and is working to expand its production capacity to support future business growth.
The Company plans to expand its nutraceutical portfolio while continuing to invest in clinical science to strengthen its branded nutraceutical ingredients.

IGL is developing Methyl Ester and advanced Oil Dispersion formulations for crop protection as a sustainable alternative to conventional hydrocarbon solvents, and has identified glycols and derivatives as candidates for Emulsifiable Concentrate formulations replacing hazardous solvents.

The Company's strategic focus on branded spirits, supported by partnerships with Bacardi and Amrut Distilleries and inclusion in defence supply channels, is expected to drive both revenue growth and margin expansion in the coming years.
